title: Remote Workers Lose 58 Minutes of Movement a Day
paragraphs: One of the things people love about working from home is that they save a lot of time — they don't have to drive through the day's slowest traffic, or walk to the bus stop and then spend an hour on the bus.
But not all of that saved time is good — a new study has found that people who work from home lose about 58 minutes of movement every day.
Researchers in Finland and Denmark looked at 97 university employees who spend some days each week working from home, and some days at the office.
Each participant wore a sensor that tracked how much they sat, walked or did other activities for seven days. They also reported what time they woke up and went to sleep each day.
On average, on days participants worked from home, they spent an extra 44 minutes sitting.

They also got 58 fewer minutes of movement and activity, and spent a little more time resting or in bed. That's not just because they didn't have to travel to work, but also because they didn't do the little things you often have to do in an office, like walk to a different room for a meeting.
The difference was biggest for people who usually walked or cycled to work.
This doesn't mean working from home is bad for your health, however.
But people who work from home might want to think about adding more movement to their workdays, the researchers said — such as standing during phone calls, or going for walks on their lunch breaks.
